author: Al Jazeera English
description:
President Donald Trump has posted on Truth Social that the United States will be hitting Iran “very hard tonight,” stating that Iran’s Navy, Air Force, radar, anti aircraft and all other defences together with its offensive capabilities are “gone”. 
He also threatened to take Kharg Island and other oil infrastructure points, assuming “total control of their oil and gas markets”, similar to the US approach in Venezuela.
Al Jazeera’s White House correspondent Kimberly Halkett noted that Trump has used such inflammatory language before, often followed by military strikes to aggressively push Iran toward a deal. She explained that the escalation was triggered by the downing of a US Apache helicopter on Tuesday, and that Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth has blamed Iran for failing to take advantage of peace opportunities. Halkett added that dissenting voices in the US Congress have argued that only Congress can declare war, but efforts to rein in the president have failed.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
The trial of two ethnic Uighur men accused of the 2015 Erawan Shrine bombing in Bangkok concludes on Thursday. The attack killed 20 people and wounded more than 100 – the deadliest in Thai history. Eleven years later, little is known about the network behind it. Victims say investigators never interviewed them. Human Rights Watch says questions remain over who ordered and carried out the attack. Thai police have refused to comment. Both suspects allege torture. There is no memorial at the shrine, and many would prefer to forget. Regardless of the verdict, the mystery is unlikely to be solved.

Al Jazeera's Tony Cheng reports from Bangkok.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
A Palestinian doctor has appeared before Israel's Supreme Court after more than 530 days in detention. Dr. Hussam Abu Safia, the director of Kamal Adwan Hospital in northern Gaza, was arrested by Israeli forces in December 2024 during a raid on the medical facility. He has reportedly been held in solitary confinement and denied medical treatment.
According to his lawyer, Nasser Odeh, Dr. Hussam remains in solitary confinement at Nafha prison. During his court appearance on Wednesday, he appeared via screen, handcuffed and shackled. Odeh reported that the court refused to remove the shackles. His client did not receive medical treatment nor the medications he needed because of a chronic illness. Odeh stated that Dr. Hussam continues to suffer severe back and neck pain as a result of an assault, and is experiencing vision problems because his glasses were confiscated and not returned.
Odeh also noted that signs of skin diseases on his hands have spread widely in sections holding politic
title: Gaza doctor Hussam Abu Safia appears before Israeli court after more than 530 days in detention

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Thousands of people marched in South Africa's KwaZulu-Natal province following a call by the MK party, led by former president Jacob Zuma, demanding that undocumented migrants leave the country. Protesters accuse foreign nationals of worsening unemployment and crime, though many others say immigrants are being wrongly blamed for South Africa's deeper economic difficulties. The demonstrations have at times turned violent, forcing hundreds of families — many from Malawi — from their homes. Nearly 3,000 displaced people are now sleeping in a Durban park, awaiting buses to take them back to Malawi.

Al Jazeera's Haru Mutasa reports from Durban, South Africa.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
The United States has launched another round of air strikes on multiple targets in Iran, hours after President Donald Trump accused Tehran of taking too long to negotiate a deal.
US Central Command described the strikes as a response to what it called Iran’s “unwarranted and continued aggression”.
Iranian media reported explosions in Bandar Abbas, Sirik and Minab in southern Iran.
In response, Iran’s Revolutionary Guard said it attacked 18 US-linked targets across the region, including military bases in Jordan, Kuwait and Bahrain. Kuwait briefly closed its airspace.
The exchanges are testing the limits of a fragile ceasefire, with both sides trading strikes for a third consecutive night.
Iran announced that the Strait of Hormuz is now closed, but US Central Command denied the claim, saying commercial shipping continues to transit the waterway. Live vessel tracking showed movement, although many ships appeared stationary.
Further explosions were reported in southern Iran, including Qes

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
President Masoud Pezeshkian has responded to remarks made by Donald Trump regarding threats to critical infrastructure. In a post on X, he said that essential systems such as transport networks, electricity, and water are the “lifeblood” of people, and that threatening them is not a display of strength but rather a sign of desperation in the face of national resilience. He added that Iran, relying on its specialists, national unity, and solidarity, will continue to stand firm against external pressure and threats.

In Washington DC, retired General Mark Kimmitt discussed the developments with Al Jazeera. In the studio, Osama bin Javaid provided further analysis on the political implications of the exchange.
